title: Add a profileId ownership check to GoalRepositoryImpl.updateGoal/deleteGoal and unify its profileId source
rule: profileId-in-PK / multi-profile isolation invariant (repository as last line of defense); naming/placement (single source of truth)
why: getGoals() filters by the constructor-injected _profileId field, but createGoal takes its own explicit profileId parameter that is never cross-checked against _profileId — the interface lets a caller create a goal 'for' a different profile than the repository instance represents, which would then be invisible to that same instance's getGoals(). Independently, updateGoal and deleteGoal load the existing row by bare goalId and mutate/delete it with no ownership check at all — updateGoal even copies existing.profileId straight back into the write (line-133, not separately confirmed) without ever comparing it to _profileId. None of this is proven to be hit by today's UI (all current call sites happen to pass matching profileIds), but the repository adds zero defense-in-depth on top of the DAO layer (which itself does not scope goalDao.updateGoal/deleteGoal/getGoalById by profile) — the next screen or bug that supplies a mismatched id/profileId pair silently edits or deletes another profile's goal.
recommendation: Pick one source of truth for 'which profile owns this repository instance' and have updateGoal/deleteGoal verify existing.profileId against it before mutating, throwing a typed error on mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: createGoal derives profileId from the same single source as the rest of the class (drop the redundant parameter or validate it against _profileId).
updateGoal and deleteGoal verify existing.profileId == _profileId before mutating/deleting, throwing a typed error otherwise.
New regression test: construct two GoalRepositoryImpl instances (one per profile) sharing one DB; assert profile B's repository cannot update or delete a goalId belonging to profile A.
